visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md (locked 2026-08-11). There is no index.html in this directory. The visual target is the six closed patterns in PUBLIC_UI.md, built from components/site/v3.
note: Homes grain fix 2026-08-14. Rhythm: THREE of the six patterns, no two adjacent alike, chrome exempt. Order is Breadcrumb, Field of the cut houses as a V3Carousel photo rail (count is a caption, never an Instrument hero), Drawing of the week's cuts, Sheet, Quiet, Footer. The empty window substitutes a Quiet for the Field and is still three patterns. Every figure comes from ONE getPriceDrops({ limit: 48, days: 7 }) call. Absent is not zero: a read that did not answer comes back degraded, the page says it could not load, Dataset / updated / count figures are omitted rather than published as 0, and refuseDegradedIsr limits that copy's ISR lifetime to 60 s (never noStore(), which is an HTTP 500 inside a Next 16 ISR render). A genuinely empty window renders the empty Quiet and caches normally. Single-family is property_sub_type 'Single Family Residence' (MARKET_TRUTH D1), not bare property type A. Drop math is previous list price to current list price. Field rows sort by lastDropPct descending. HideAwareListingGrid is a declared deletion: hidden-home subtraction stays on /search. SITE-70: photographs open via shadcn-carousel -> V3Carousel; ItemList JSON-LD lists the cut homes.

KbListingMap: replaced by the Field's built-in plot of rows that carry coordinates.

HideAwareListingGrid: the per-user hidden-aware ListingCard grid (W7.2). Hidden-home subtraction stays on /search. This page is a curated 7-day cut list, not a browse of for-sale inventory, and it does not import a raw listing renderer.
Neighborhood mini-table: the 7-day pull grouped by subdivision. Field row meta still names displaySubdivision when the feed has a readable name.
City chip sections: the filter-nav and every-city chip rows. City doors live in the closing Quiet.
KbCommunityAlerts markup: replaced by PriceDropAlertsSheet on V3Sheet. Capture contract unchanged (see dataLayer), including the company honeypot.
KbSell: the seller band. Seller ask lives on Sell. The house is the primary on this buyer Field.
CTABar: the closing talk-to-a-broker bar. Not carried.
V3Instrument number hero: 60 / $3.2M / 5.6% and the method essay. Count is a caption beside the Field.
DisplayHeading / PageBreadcrumb hidden parity hacks on the city route.

dataLayer.getPriceDrops: lib/data/listings/getPriceDrops.ts. { limit: 48, days: 7 }. No .catch() empty swallow. `total` is the whole window, `cap` is the list cap the drawing states, and `degraded: true` (the read did not answer) renders the could-not-load Quiet with no count and calls refuseDegradedIsr, never noStore(). THE ONLY READ ON THIS PAGE.

Contract: { email, filters: DROPS_ALERT_FILTERS { propertyType: 'A', propertySubTypes: 'Single Family Residence' }, plus { city } on a city page, company }, so the alert follows the single-family population the page lists.

competitiveTarget: Beat Zillow's and Redfin's price-cut filters on a page a search engine can actually rank. Their reductions live behind a filter state with no indexable URL; this is a standing page for 'price reductions bend oregon' and 'price drops central oregon' that publishes the cut homes themselves, each one a door, with the source trace and the refresh stamp under the set. The answer -- how many homes cut price and by how much -- is in text, not only in the list.

First viewport, scale 1, palette-quantized, against the listing-dial fix tree's own next build + next start (2026-09-30).

tasteReview.beats: Redfin's 'Price Reduced' filtered list — this page wins on showing the actual shape of the week's cuts (the beeswarm dot plot, smallest to deepest, with a stated median) and a per-city bar breakdown a portal filter never surfaces; it loses on browsable depth, since only 48 of 191 cuts are shown and there's no map or further paging.

defects.finding: The layout lock calls for the field of cut houses up front with count as a caption; instead the page opens straight into a single large house plus a comps sidebar (V3ListingDial), and a true field/mosaic of multiple cut-house photographs never appears anywhere across all eight captured states.

defects.section: ALL CUTS / UNDER 5% / 5 TO 10% / 10% AND UP tabs
defects.finding: The band selector is four gray tiles showing a bold count under a label with no sentence telling a buyer what a given band means for them — reads as a KPI grid even though the tiles are functional filters.

Scrolled to the city-breakdown state at 375px, the prior section's comp row is sliced mid-line under the sticky header — a partial '-5.0% -4.9% -4.9%' fragment is visible with no spacing buffer above the tab bar.
Three rows of tiny thumbnail plus price plus delta plus address is generic portal-sidebar furniture with no visual encoding beyond a small photo; it is the least distinctive element on the page.

tasteReview.verdict: This is a competently sourced, correctly-plumbed price-drop page (every figure traces to Oregon Data Share with a fetch date and a 'how we calculate this' disclosure) wearing a single-house ListingDial hero where the layout lock demands a field of cut houses — demoMatch is false because no catalog interaction is present at all, this is a bespoke component, and the mosaic the lock specifies never shows up. Inventory context (191 cuts, 48 shown, per-city counts, a real distribution chart) is a genuine information increment over a flat list, so honesty/function holds, but originality and design quality are capped by the KPI-tile band selector and a dull, un-encoded comps sidebar that any portal already ships. Fix the opening to an actual field of house photographs before this clears the taste floor.

contentFloor.note: No-regression floor (ci:route-content-floor). A build under any number here fails before the evaluator runs. Lower a number only by hand, in the same commit, with the reason. heroImageNatural LOWERED 648 -> 576 (2026-09-23, PR #352 blocker): the winner is a Spark MLS listing photo requested at the sanctioned 800x600 bucket; its delivered resolution is Spark's per-photo derivative, which PR #351 measured across 24 live assets at 640 to 853px, never under 640. The 2026-09-12 seed happened to read a 720px derivative; CI on 2026-09-23 read 640 on two runs. 576 = floor(640 * 0.9), the same floor PR #351 set for the same photo bucket on oregon-city and place-type-community. The banned 320x240 thumb would still read 320 and fail. heroImageNatural LOWERED 576 -> 420 (2026-09-23, PR #352): 576 assumed Spark never returns a lead photo under 640; CI run 35877907272 read 496 on /oregon/medford (a live listing's 800x600-bucket derivative). The floor exists to catch the banned 320x240 ledger thumb, which production /homes-for-sale?view=list served at 320 to 376 natural on 2026-09-23. Lead derivatives are now observed at 496 to 853. 420 sits between the two populations: a thumb still fails, a small lead does not. Set on all three classes whose winner is that same Spark lead bucket (oregon-city, place-type-community, price-drops). words LOWERED 1267 -> 747 (2026-09-24, SITE-195, Matt: every listing carousel becomes the listing dial): the floor counts visible words in <main> (innerText), and the carousel it was seeded on kept every slide's copy visible-but-scrolled, so each of the fold's 48 houses counted its city, price, drop line, address and specs. V3ListingDial serves every house's card in the HTML (each still an <a href>, its copy intact) but hides the cards not showing, so innerText now reads the shown house plus a price and street per thumbnail. Measured on this branch's production build: HEAD 1906 words, the dial 1068, with 1849 words of card copy present in the served HTML inside the hidden cards (every band's dial). No house, figure or link left the page. 747 = floor(1068 * 0.7), the gate's own words tolerance.
